ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, sliced 7 mm thick or left whole and butterflied
thumb ginger , grated — ginger works harder here than in the beef lanes
/2 tsp black pepper ; 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
Steamed rice , lettuce ssam, ssamjang , kimchi , scallion threads

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Medium-high fire, single layer, slices not touching. Chicken's surface water steams before it browns if the pan is crowded — space is crust.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the first side is undisturbed until the edges turn opaque and the underside is browned, about 2 minutes for slices, 4 for butterflied whole thighs.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Flip once; the second side runs 1–2 minutes more for slices. Pull when the meat's juices run clear at a thick piece's cut edge and the surface is glossy brown — no pinkness anywhere, chicken's absolute rule.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: test piece: glossy, tender, sweet-savory with ginger brightening the finish — chicken's mildness is the marinade's showcase, and every ingredient reads clearly here.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Scissors into bite pieces, sesame and scallion over, warm platter. Ssam or rice bowl, both lanes open.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the rice bowl test: juice over rice first — the pan will have a glossy glaze of rendered fat and marinade that spoons like a sauce, milder and rounder than the beef version. That spoon is the record's quiet prize.

storageNotes: Marinated chicken keeps 24 hours. Cooked, 3 days — cold slices over rice, or the weeknight bossam-style wrap with ssamjang.
Variations: the gochujang fork (#M17); the same marinade on wing segments glazed in the last minutes; pineapple swapped for pear in a pinch (shorter window — its enzyme is far stronger).
